Subject: clone `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/5dbc61f3-e21d-5874-a6a8-3a991f0f402c/scratchpad/exec/t-024`, `fb6344e..6c93bf5`. Clone left clean at 6c93bf5; its `data/guidebook.db` sha256 unmoved across my runs. My scratch (`.../scratchpad/critic-t024/`) is deleted.

**One thing I left behind and could not remove:** `/t.db`, a 0-byte file at the filesystem root. A probe script of mine ran with an unset variable, so `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH` resolved to `/t.db` and `db.py` created it. The harness safety check refused my `rm`. It needs deleting by a person.

## Findings (worst first)

**1. HIGH — T024-01, the only test of the seed, is skipped silently in CI.**
- Artifact: `scripts/tests/test_db_amend_writers.py:1936-1953`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml:173-183`.
- Claim: the seed is gated against the enum's members derived from git history, with fetch-depth 0.
- Failure case: the `tests` job checks out with bare `actions/checkout@v4`, which is depth 1. `fetch-depth: 0` sits only on `classify`, `governance` and `attestation` (lines 72, 209, 229). At depth 1 the history walk finds no `class JurisdictionCode`, the case prints `SKIPPED-NO-FIXTURE` and calls no `record()`, so the file exits 0 with one fewer assertion.
- Command: `git clone --depth 1 --no-checkout file://<clone> x; cd x; git log --format=%H -- schemas/enums.py | wc -l` gives 1; `git show <that>:schemas/enums.py | grep -c "class JurisdictionCode"` gives 0.
- The check is `level: advisory` with `no_floor` (`governance/check-registry.yaml:1076-1086`), so nothing escalates the lost case.

**2. MEDIUM — "red on the base except three precondition cases" (commit message) is not supported by the artifact.**
- Artifact: `.../scratchpad/guidebook-t-024/red-on-base.txt`.
- Failure case A: it shows `T024-00` and `T024-01` green and `EXAMINED: 184`. On the real base neither can run: there is no `dbcore.declared_jurisdictions` and no `base_jurisdictions`. A file where the swept J-cases (which assert the new message text) pass and the seed test is green was run against head's `dbcore.py` and a migrated database, with only `db.py`'s verb absent.
- Failure case B: T024-01 is the seed assertion, not a precondition, and it has never been shown red.
- Reproduced two ways on a true `fb6344e` checkout (sparse shared clone):
  - the task's own route (head test file copied onto base) dies with `AttributeError: module 'dbcore' has no attribute 'declared_jurisdictions'` at line 1446, before any T024 case;
  - base's original file with only the T024 block spliced in dies with the same error at the block's first line (`DECL0 = ...`).
- Both give zero `T024-` lines, no `EXAMINED:` line, and a traceback. A crash is not 20 cases shown red.

**3. MEDIUM — `admission_ref` is written and then read by no check; "NULL marks exactly the seeded set" rests only on the case in finding 1.**
- Artifact: `scripts/db.py` `add_jurisdiction` (row dict about line 7890); `scripts/migrations/129_jurisdiction_registry.sql` header lines 15-17.
- `git grep -n admission_ref -- scripts schemas skills governance` returns the writer and the test only.
- The verb this copies has an at-rest validator: `scripts/validate_parameters.py:97-112` re-counts `terms.catalogue_approval_ref` with `ledger_heading_count`. Nothing does that for `base_jurisdictions.admission_ref`.
- Failure cases, each with nothing going red: a row landed by a data migration with NULL `admission_ref` (the column is nullable) is indistinguishable from seed; a ledger heading later edited or duplicated leaves a dangling pointer.
- The pointer is stored, not merely printed. My scratch row: `('US-CA','sub-national','US','Owner answers 2026-11-13 (tenth set) — …','2026-11-13 07:22','s')`. Your brief said "checked and printed but not stored, as designed"; the task file (section 4 item 2) says stored, and the code stores it.

**4. MEDIUM — admitting a code moved from a reviewed tooling PR to a verb any session can satisfy with an unrelated heading.**
- Artifact: `scripts/dbcore.py` `check_jurisdiction` refusal text; `scripts/db.py` `add_jurisdiction`.
- The base refusal read: "an owner decision recorded in the enum, with its ruling, in a tooling PR (CLAUDE.md rule 10)". Head reads: "record it in references/project-standards.md, then `db.py add-jurisdiction --approval-ref <that heading>`".
- Failure case: I admitted `US-CA` and dry-ran `AR` (one of the 17) against the last dated heading in the ledger, "Owner answers 2026-11-13 (tenth set) — the T-4 agreement rules …", which says nothing about jurisdictions. Both were accepted.
- Headings of entries that are explicitly not the owner's words also qualify, e.g. "Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-01 …", while the docstring says the pointer is "the ledger entry that records the owner's approval".
- `dbcore.writable_tables(conn)` includes `base_jurisdictions`, so the row ships in a research batch's data migration.
- The task records this as an "accepted limitation". It still sits against "without weakening a refusal": the scope control is now procedural, and per finding 3 unchecked afterwards.

**5. MEDIUM (latent) — the roll-up reaches coverage only; the engine's distinct-jurisdiction richness test still treats a sub-national code as a separate jurisdiction.**
- Artifact: `scripts/assess/assess_cell.py:1147-1164` (`_distinct_jurisdictions`) and `:1190-1199`, reading `src["jurisdiction"]` (`:1102`).
- Owner's OD-04 text (`references/project-standards.md:5949`): "a sub-national instrument counts toward its country and owes no coverage alone".
- Failure case: `_distinct_jurisdictions([{'jurisdiction':'US'},{'jurisdiction':'US-CA'}])` returns `{'us','us-ca'}`. Once a sub-national row exists and T-113 re-files sources with `amend-source --field jurisdiction`, one country's federal and state instruments satisfy ">=2 T4-5 sources, distinct jurisdictions" and count toward ">=3 T6 codes from N distinct jurisdictions".
- No sub-national row exists in this PR, so nothing renders differently today. This PR supplies the verb and vocabulary that make it reachable, and the task's reader list ("exactly these readers") does not name this one.

**6. LOW-MEDIUM — the verb's code-shape refusals have gaps; all of these were accepted on `--dry-run`, rc 0.**
- `--code US-CA --kind country`: a dashed sub-national code filed as a country with no parent, so the roll-up never applies to it.
- `--code "US-" --kind sub-national --parent US`: empty subdivision.
- `--code "A R"`, `--code "-" --kind meta`, `--code 123`, `--code ARGENTINA`.
- `--session nonexistent-session`: the session is not resolved against anything.
- The table CHECK is only `= UPPER(...) AND NOT LIKE 'GB%'`, so the schema admits them too.
- The schema also does not hold "a parent must be a `country`" or the `<parent>-` prefix; those live in the verb alone, so a data migration can land a sub-national row whose parent is meta or sub-national.

**7. LOW — prose callers left false (rule 4 / 7a; no gate covers them).**
- `governance/pipeline-contract.yaml:49`: "the architecture note's base.jurisdictions, which has no table yet". The table now exists, and this is the `references:` of the criterion both jurisdiction checks cite as `basis`.
- `governance/conceptual-model.md:37`: "| ENT-13 | **Jurisdiction** | DONE (enum) | — |". The diff edited another line of this file and left this one.
- `workplan/pipeline-state-graph/ATOMS.tsv` ENT-339, ENT-368, ENT-378 (and `atoms/atoms-ent.jsonl:296,325,335`) quote verbatim three `governance/jurisdiction-philosophy.md` lines this diff rewrote. `build_graph.py --check` reports the same failure count on base and head (109 in real checkouts) only because it reads the quotes of cited atoms (`EXAMINED: 362 atoms whose quote was read` of 2566). These three had no subject. The task excludes `workplan/` from the sweep; the staleness is real regardless.
- `workplan/pipeline-state-graph/graph.json` lists 72 of the 73 `add_parser` verbs in `db.py`; the one missing is `add-jurisdiction`. Not regenerated, not flagged.

**8. LOW — literals that go stale with nothing red (rule 7a).**
- The migration number is typed in three non-migration files: `scripts/dbcore.py` (`declared_jurisdictions` docstring, "below migration 129"), `scripts/audit/jurisdiction_db_vocabulary.py` (comment, "below migration 129"), `governance/conceptual-model.md` ("a table since migration 129"). The number will be re-derived after the concurrent merges; these sentences are swept by no gate.
- `scripts/db.py` comment above `_AMENDABLE_SVE_FIELDS`: "the four sub-national instruments", a corpus count typed into code.

**9. LOW — per-code admission provenance left the live tree.**
- The deleted enum carried, per code, the ruling that admitted it (2026-09-18 for BE/ES/HR/IT; 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-01 for PT/FI/UN; owner decision D2 for UG, with "declaring UG licenses no further Ugandan research").
- The migration header says "this header is its record" but names none of those rulings or dates, only "the enum's comments cite several rulings". The record is now git history only.
- `NAME_TO_CODE` (27 codes) and the philosophy tables (27 codes) both lack BE, ES, FI, HR, INT, IT, PT, UG, UN.
